report.summary: Transfer 500s and multi-second latency coincide with DB lock waits caused by an idle-in-transaction session. Outbox delivery, consumer and pool look healthy. The 500 mechanism itself was not observed.

findings.claim: Transfers show 36 of 495 requests failing with 500 (7.3%), with p95 1.56 s and p99 2.94 s.
findings.reason: Request metrics are complete and show both the server errors and the latency tail.

findings.claim: Sessions were blocked behind an 'idle in transaction' session (62553) from 16:20:06 to 16:20:52, with waits up to about 2 s.
findings.reason: Historical blocker samples show ledger_app sessions waiting on this session across many samples.

findings.claim: The lock waits likely explain the slow transfers, and possibly the 500s. The blocking window matches when pool connections were active.
findings.reason: The blocking window (16:20:06-16:20:52) overlaps the active-connection window (16:20:08-16:20:53). The pool had no timeouts or pending borrowers, so it is not the bottleneck.

limitations: Blocker sampling is every 2 s, and 500 error timestamps and messages were not available, so a direct link between blocking and the 500s is not shown.
The identity and origin of session 62553 (role 'other') were not determined.
next_checks: Identify session 62553 (application name, query, transaction start) and why it is left idle in transaction.
Correlate 500 error timestamps and logs with the 16:20:06-16:20:52 blocking window.

alternatives.reason: All 445 deliveries succeeded on attempt 1 in about 71 ms. Arrivals match publications, with no failures and a tiny backlog.
alternatives.hypothesis: Outbox/consumer delivery slowness causes the failures

alternatives.reason: There were 0 acquisition timeouts, 0 pending borrowers, a max of 3 active connections out of 10, and acquire time under 4 ms.
alternatives.hypothesis: Connection pool exhaustion causes the failures and slowness

findings.claim: Transfers show 7.3% HTTP 500s (36 of 495) and a p95 of 1.56 s / p99 2.94 s.

findings.claim: The idle-in-transaction lock holder probably caused the slow transfers and some of the 500s; the pool was not the limit.

limitations: Blocker sampling is every 2 s, and the blocker session's owner and statement are unknown.
